notice: Producer research decision only. Independent review and owner adoption remain separate.
rationale: I read the complete held EO 13572 (76 FR 24787, May 3, 2011): blocks property of persons responsible for human-rights abuses in Syria, expands the scope of the emergency declared in EO 13338, with Treasury/State implementing authority; no own term. I read the held EO 14312 (90 FR 29395, July 3, 2025, 'Providing for the Revocation of Syria Sanctions'): sec. 3(a) 'Effective July 1, 2025, I hereby terminate the national emergency declared in Executive Order 13338 ... and revoke that order, as well as Executive Order 13399, Executive Order 13460, Executive Order 13572 of April 29, 2011 (Blocking Property of Certain Persons with Respect to Human Rights Abuses in Syria), Executive Order 13573, and Executive Order 13582.' Sec. 3(b) (NEA sec. 202(a)) preserves only actions taken or pending proceedings, acts before July 1, 2025 and matured rights or penalties, not any continuing prohibition. Sec. 4 of EO 14312 expands the different emergency of EO 13894 and does not reinstate EO 13572. Partial scope: the revocation names EO 13572 outright with no exception. D6 (later events): EO 13573 (May 18, 2011) and EO 13582 (Aug. 17, 2011) refer to EO 13572 as having expanded the scope of the EO 13338 emergency; they add measures on the same emergency and are themselves revoked by sec. 3(a), so they do not extend EO 13572 beyond July 1, 2025. EO 13338, 13399 and 13460 (the history's cross-references) are revoked in the same sec. 3(a); I used their texts only as context and did not need them for the basis. I read all of EO 13572 (secs. 1-11, effective Apr. 29, 2011, no term) and secs. 1-4 of EO 14312, and the passages in which EO 13573 and EO 13582 cite EO 13572. No held order after July 2025 names EO 13572 (searched), so there is no revival. The history's eCFR 'current-law lead' is a pointer without a held text and is not used. Provisional NO hypothesis only.
